rejected.title: Society steering science
card: Science does not happen in isolation. Society influences which research goes ahead and how it is done.
Public concern
When many people worry about a problem, such as climate change, there is pressure to study it. Governments and groups may respond.
Funding
Research costs money. Projects that governments, businesses or charities pay for are more likely to go ahead.
Ethics
Ethics is about what is right and wrong. It can limit research, such as rules on how genetic tests can be used so that people's private information is protected.
rejected.remember: Public concern, funding and ethics help decide which research goes ahead and how.

a.q: A government sets aside money for research into protecting the Great Barrier Reef after public concern. Which factor is most directly shown?
opts: Funding directing research towards a problem
Ethics banning a type of experiment
Peer review finding an error in a study
A new tool making new data possible
a.why: The money from the government sends research towards the reef, which shows funding. Public concern started the response, but no ethical limit or error check is described.
a.clue: Look for what the government actually provided.

b.q: A company can test a person's genes for disease risk. A law then limits how insurers may use the results, to protect privacy. Which factor is most directly shown?
opts: Ethics limiting how genetic test results are used
Funding paying for more genetic testing research
Public concern pushing for more genetic research
A new machine making genetic data possible to collect
b.why: The law is based on what is right and wrong, protecting people's private information, so it shows ethics limiting how science is used. It tempts to pick public concern, but the law sets a limit rather than pushing for more research. No money or new machine is described.
b.clue: Does the law add research or set a limit?

b.q: A company can test a person's genes for disease risk, but a law limits how insurers may use the results. What does this show?
opts: Ethics and society can limit how science is applied
Science cannot produce reliable genetic data
Research is decided only by what scientists want
Funding is the only factor that shapes research

version.title: Society steering science
card: Science does not happen in isolation. Society influences which research goes ahead and how it is done.
Public concern
When many people worry about a problem, such as climate change, there is pressure to study it. Governments and groups may respond.
Funding
Research costs money. Projects that governments, businesses or charities pay for are more likely to go ahead.
Ethics

Ethics is about what is right and wrong. It can limit research itself: a study that tests people's genes needs approval from an ethics committee, which can stop it or set conditions such as consent and privacy.
version.remember: Public concern, funding and ethics help decide which research goes ahead and how.

a.q: After public worry about coral bleaching, a government sets aside money for Great Barrier Reef research. Which factor most directly sends research to the reef here?
opts: Funding sending research towards a problem
Ethics rules stopping a kind of experiment on reefs
Peer review finding a mistake in an earlier study
A new tool letting scientists gather reef data
a.why: The government's money sends research towards the reef, which shows funding. Public concern started the response, but no ethical limit, error check or new tool is described.
a.clue: Look for what the government actually provided.

b.q: Researchers plan to test the genes of 500 volunteers for a disease risk. A university review panel lets the study go ahead only if every volunteer agrees in writing and their results are kept private. Which factor is most directly shown?
opts: Ethics setting limits on how a study is run
Funding deciding which study gets paid for
Public concern pushing a problem up the agenda
A new machine making genetic data possible
b.why: The panel is judging what is right for the volunteers, so its conditions show ethics limiting how the research is done. Public concern is tempting, but no wider worry pushed for this study. No money or new machine is described.
b.clue: Think about why the panel cares about the volunteers' consent and privacy.

a.best: Funding sending research towards a problem

b.best: Ethics setting limits on how a study is run
